title: Machine learning guides refinement of DNA aptamers binding NGAL
summary: Neural models trained on particle-display affinity-screening data guided sequence mutation and candidate nomination, followed by synthesis and experimental affinity testing. The authors report a 23-nucleotide truncation of candidate G13 with measured dissociation constant 1.5 nM, compared with about 8 nM for the full-length parent under their assay. This is a binding result, not demonstrated diagnostic or therapeutic efficacy. The screening set is not 187,499 independently validated agents; sequence-level prior art remains open.
ai_technology: Neural-network models trained on particle-display affinity data

source_review.scope: Primary publisher indexed full text, article dates, methods/results, affiliations and disclosed limitations.

evidence.tested: The study reports particle-display screening and measured NGAL binding, including full Kd for truncated and parent G13.
evidence.unknown: Binding assay only; no diagnostic/therapeutic outcome; one holdout set used for tuning and sequence novelty requires further review.
evidence.ai_role: Trained neural models extrapolated from experimentally measured sequences to nominate and iteratively refine higher-affinity DNA aptamers and truncations.
